description:
Magu Cha is a green tea counted among the famous teas of Jiangxi, but it is rarely described in any detail. The name suggests a link with Mount Magu at Nancheng, in Jiangxi, although that connection is an inference here and not a documented fact.

Little is documented about how it is made or what makes it distinct. Taking it as a typical Jiangxi green, you would expect heat-fixed leaf with a fresh, mellow cup.

Brew it as you would any spring green: water around 80 °C and short steeps, adjusting by taste.

If you find it for sale, ask the seller where the garden is, how it is processed and when it was picked. With so little on record, treat those answers as the real label.
history: Little is documented. It appears on modern lists of Jiangxi's well-known teas, but who developed it, when, and how it has changed are not clearly recorded.
